subject: Finova private SIEM onboarding: ingress/egress, tracing hooks, and chain-of-custody
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 09 Jan 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Finova private SIEM onboarding — evidence & network gating checklist

Team —

Finova (Asha/Luis) asked us to produce a compact SIEM onboarding package for their private VPC deployment this week. Goal: provide everything their security team needs to accept log + trace exports into their Splunk HEC collector and confirm chain-of-custody for evidence transfer.

Top-level asks from Finova:
- Sample log bundle (application + inference runtime) with PII redaction notes
- Splunk HEC config example + recommended events mapping
- Network CIDR / port allowlist + egress constraints for evidence transfer
- Trace hook contract (span naming, sampling, correlation ids)
- Evidence custody checklist & transfer receipts (who signs, retention windows)

Meeting scheduled with Finova on Thursday 2028-01-12 10:00 PT — they want the package 24h prior.

Immediate owners:
- Kimberly: logs/PII redaction & sample bundle
- Marissa: trace hook contract + span examples for their observability team
- Ben: network diagram + egress/ingress rules (IAC snippets ok)

I've attached a starter evidence-checklist.xlsx and a rough network-cidr-diagram.png. Please reply with one-line confirmations and any blockers by EOD Tuesday. I will consolidate and forward to Asha/Luis on Wednesday morning.

Thanks —
Mateo
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-cidr-diagram.png (image)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Finova private SIEM onboarding — evidence & network gating checklist

Thanks Mateo — confirmed, I can own the log bundle. Quick notes / questions: 

- For PII redaction, do we ship a sanitized sample (production-scrubbed) or a synthetic equivalent? Finova has strict retention rules, they prefer sanitized samples where possible.
- I'll generate a 48-hour sample from the inference runtime and include the redaction mapping. Will that satisfy their SOC reviewer?
- For Splunk HEC: I have a minimal splunk-hec-config.json that demonstrates token headers, index routing, and backpressure retry semantics. I'll attach that as a stub.
- Also need the target HEC endpoint: do we put the typical https://hec.finova.internal:8088 or will they give a shared ingestion host?

Action items: I will produce:
1) sanitized-sample-logs.tar.gz (48h, two apps + runtime)
2) splunk-hec-config.json (example + comments)
3) short README describing redaction approach

Ben — can you confirm the CIDR space and whether Finova expects a source NAT IP vs. per-node egress? That affects the firewall snippet I include.

-Kim
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: splunk-hec-config.json (text)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@finovabank.com>, Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@finovabank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Finova private SIEM onboarding — evidence & network gating checklist

Asha / Luis —

Forwarding our internal plan so you can see the deliverables ahead of the call on Thursday. High-level package we will deliver by 2028-01-11 10:00 PT: 

1) sanitized-sample-logs.tar.gz — 48-hour sample covering inference runtime (tokenization, request/response events), API gateway access logs, and worker metrics. Each file will include a redaction manifest.
2) splunk-hec-config.json — recommended event format, index hints, and example token header handling (includes idempotency and retry guidance).
3) trace-hooks-contract.md — span name conventions, correlators (request_id => trace_id mapping), suggested sampling rates for production vs. debug windows.
4) network-cidr-diagram.png + firewall snippets — we propose a single NATed egress IP (10.12.0.34) to simplify Finova ACLs, or alternatively we can provide per-node egress ranges if you need per-host mapping.
5) evidence-checklist.xlsx + custody receipts template — point of contact, signatures, hash values, retention periods (30/90/365 day options).

Open questions for you prior to the call: 
- Preferred HEC endpoint and token rotation cadence?
- Do you require a signed custody receipt for each evidence transfer or a batch weekly digest?
- Any constraints on TLS ciphers / mutual TLS for the HEC endpoint? We can support mTLS if Finova's HSM issues a cert.

We attached the draft splunk-hec-config.json and network-cidr-diagram.png for your review. If helpful, Splunk's onboarding team (onboard@splunk.com) is copied on this thread and can join to discuss HEC-side tuning.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

—Mateo
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: splunk-hec-config.json (text), network-cidr-diagram.png (image)

From: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@finovabank.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Finova private SIEM onboarding — evidence & network gating checklist

Mateo / team —

Thanks for the clear plan and the early draft artifacts. This is close to what our SOC needs. A couple of clarifications before the meeting: 

1) Evidence custody: we require a signed receipt per transfer for high-fidelity audit windows (we can accept a batched weekly digest for lower-risk exports). For the initial onboarding send, please include an example signed receipt for the sanitized-sample-logs.tar.gz.
2) mTLS: preferred on HEC endpoints. We will provide a short-lived cert for the POC and our CA details. Please include instructions for both token-based and mTLS ingestion in the splunk-hec-config.json (we can fallback to token if mTLS fails).
3) NAT vs per-node: NATed egress is easiest for our firewall team; confirm the proposed IP (10.12.0.34) and a plan for rotation if you need to retire that address.

Can someone from Redwood confirm the hash algorithm you will use for evidence receipts (SHA256 preferred) and whether transfers will include a signed timestamp? We'll add that to our acceptance checklist.

I'll bring Finova's Splunk lead to the call; Luis will follow up with an internal ticket for any additional infra constraints.

Best,
Asha Reddy
Head of Platform Security
Finova Bank

Attachment: finova-evidence-request.pdf (PDF)
